use: For something moving by itself; moving something yourself is ugokasu.

example.ja: 動かないで！写真撮るから。
example.english: Don't move! I'm taking a photo.

examplePolite.ja: 動かないでください。写真を撮ります。
examplePolite.english: Please don't move. I'm taking a photo.

notes: Also for machines: pasokon ga ugokanai (my computer won't work).

english: have someone with you; take or bring someone along
use: For people and animals, mostly as tsureteru (has with them) or inside tsurete iku and tsurete kuru.

example.romaji: ano hito, itsumo inu tsureteru ne.
example.ja: あの人、いつも犬連れてるね。
example.english: That guy always has his dog with him.

examplePolite.romaji: ano kata wa itsumo inu o tsurete imasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: あの方はいつも犬を連れていますね。
examplePolite.english: That person always has a dog with them.

notes: Things you carry use motsu instead: motte iku, motte kuru.

english: get on, ride (a train, bus, car, bike)
use: The vehicle takes ni: densha ni noru.

example.ja: 次の電車に乗ろう。
example.english: Let's get on the next train.

examplePolite.ja: 次の電車に乗りましょう。

notes: Opposite: oriru (get off).

use: The seat takes ni: isu ni suwaru.

example.ja: この席、座ってもいい？
example.english: Can I sit here?

examplePolite.romaji: kono seki, suwatte mo ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: この席、座ってもいいですか？

notes: Opposite: tatsu (stand up). Hosts say douzo, okake kudasai (please have a seat).

example.ja: 駅まで歩いて行こうか。
example.english: Shall we walk to the station?

examplePolite.ja: 駅まで歩いて行きましょうか。
examplePolite.english: Shall we walk to the station?

notes: aruite gofun = a five-minute walk.

use: For what a customer, boss or elder does; never for yourself.

example.romaji: buchou wa mou kaigi ni irasshatta?
example.ja: 部長はもう会議にいらっしゃった？
example.english: Has the boss come to the meeting yet?

examplePolite.romaji: buchou wa mou kaigi ni irasshaimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 部長はもう会議にいらっしゃいましたか？
examplePolite.english: Has the department head arrived at the meeting yet?

notes: irasshaimase is the shop greeting; irasshai is a warm 'welcome' at home.

example.ja: 急いで！電車行っちゃうよ。
example.english: Hurry! We'll miss the train.

examplePolite.romaji: isoide kudasai. densha ga demasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 急いでください。電車が出ますよ。
examplePolite.english: Please hurry. The train's about to leave.

notes: isoganakute ii yo = no rush.

example.ja: 走れば間に合うよ！
example.english: If we run, we'll make it!

examplePolite.ja: 走れば間に合いますよ。
examplePolite.english: If we run, we'll make it.

notes: Also for vehicles running: basu ga hashitte nai (the buses aren't running).

use: Something stops by itself; stopping something yourself is tomeru.

example.ja: 電車、また途中で止まっちゃった。
example.english: The train's stopped partway again.

examplePolite.romaji: densha ga mata tochuu de tomatte shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 電車がまた途中で止まってしまいました。
examplePolite.english: The train has stopped partway again.

notes: Same sound as 泊まる tomaru, stay the night: hoteru ni tomaru.

example.ja: 7時に駅前に集まろう。
example.english: Let's meet in front of the station at seven.

examplePolite.ja: 7時に駅前に集まりましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's meet in front of the station at seven.

notes: Collecting things or rounding people up is atsumeru.

example.romaji: ano inu ni chikazukanai hou ga ii yo.
example.ja: あの犬に近づかない方がいいよ。
example.english: Better not go near that dog.

examplePolite.romaji: ano inu ni wa chikazukanai hou ga ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの犬には近づかない方がいいですよ。
examplePolite.english: You'd better not go near that dog.

notes: Also for time drawing near: shiken ga chikazuite kita (the exam is coming up).

english: go regularly (to school, work, a gym); commute
use: For a place you keep going to, usually as kayotte iru.

example.romaji: ima jimu ni kayotteru n da.
example.ja: 今ジムに通ってるんだ。
example.english: I'm going to a gym these days.

examplePolite.ja: 今ジムに通っています。
examplePolite.english: I go to a gym these days.

notes: A single trip is just iku.

example.ja: 雪で飛行機飛ばないって。
example.english: They say the planes aren't flying because of the snow.

examplePolite.romaji: yuki de hikouki ga tobanai sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 雪で飛行機が飛ばないそうです。
examplePolite.english: I hear flights are grounded because of the snow.

notes: sugu tonde iku = I'll rush right over. A jump on the spot is often janpu suru.

english: come here (to a child or pet)
use: Warm and parental; to an adult friend say kotchi kite instead.

example.ja: ほら、おいで。こっちおいで。
example.english: Come on, come over here.

notes: Also an older person's invitation: asobi ni oide (come and visit).

use: mairimasu humbly says you're going or coming, to customers or a boss; maitta (na) is a casual 'ugh, I'm stuck'.

example.ja: 参ったな、鍵なくしちゃった。
example.english: Ugh, I've lost my keys.

examplePolite.romaji: mairimashita. kagi o nakushite shimatta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 参りました。鍵をなくしてしまったんです。
examplePolite.english: I'm in a bind. I've lost my keys.

notes: In service speech: sugu mairimasu (I'll be right with you).

english: get off (a train, bus); go down
use: The vehicle takes o: densha o oriru.

example.romaji: tsugi no eki de oriru yo.
example.ja: 次の駅で降りるよ。
example.english: We're getting off at the next station.

examplePolite.english: I'm getting off at the next station.

notes: Opposite: noru. On a packed train, orimasu! gets people to let you out.

english: go out (on an outing or errand)

example.ja: ちょっと出かけてくるね。
example.english: I'm popping out for a bit.

examplePolite.ja: ちょっと出かけてきます。
examplePolite.english: I'm going out for a bit.

notes: dekakete iru = is out (not home right now).

english: get out of the way, move aside
use: doite! (move!) is blunt; with strangers say sumimasen instead.

example.ja: ちょっとどいて、通れないよ。
example.english: Move a sec, I can't get through.

examplePolite.ja: すみません、ちょっとどいてもらえますか？
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, could you move over a little?

notes: doke! is the rough command. Moving something else out of the way is dokeru.

english: line up, queue; be in a row

example.romaji: kono mise, itsumo sugoi naranderu ne.
example.ja: この店、いつもすごい並んでるね。
example.english: This place always has a huge line.

examplePolite.romaji: kono mise wa itsumo sugoku narande imasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: この店はいつもすごく並んでいますね。
examplePolite.english: There's always a long line at this place.

notes: Arranging things in a row is naraberu.

example.romaji: kinou, inu ni oikakerareta n da yo!
example.ja: 昨日、犬に追いかけられたんだよ！
example.english: A dog chased me yesterday!

examplePolite.ja: 昨日、犬に追いかけられました。
examplePolite.english: I was chased by a dog yesterday.

notes: Also chasing a dream: yume o oikakeru.
